final_rationale: The verdict does not change. The Actor narrowed the claim from clean compliance to caveated compliance, but supplied no new admissible evidence. That reframing is directionally more accurate and proportional, yet the policy text is a present-tense predicate: certification may proceed only if current release documentation reflects current evaluation results and material segment weaknesses are disclosed or covered by an approved mitigation. On the available record, those predicates are not shown as satisfied. A caveated future-looking path to compliance is not the same as present compliance, even with caveats. Aggregate readiness passes and the absence of severity-one rehearsal incidents support operational readiness context, but they do not cure the unresolved documentation and disclosure requirements for certification.
remaining_concerns: No admissible evidence shows the current release documentation has been updated to reflect the current evaluation results.
The multilingual customer-support slice remains a material limitation for a named launch use case and there is no evidence it has been disclosed in current release documentation.
The release record still appears to contain only informal monitoring commentary, not approved mitigation or reviewed risk acceptance.
Prior approval of the model family remains contextual only and does not establish compliance for the current release after the retrieval configuration change.
